#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Home appliance energy cost estimator (Python 3 standard library only).

Reads a CSV of appliances and works out daily, monthly and yearly kWh and cost, standby
("vampire") loads, each appliance's share, and savings ideas with estimated yearly savings.

CSV columns (header required; comma or semicolon; only the first three are required):
  appliance        name, e.g. "Fridge-freezer" (keywords drive the savings ideas)
  watts            power while running (nameplate or plug-in meter), per unit
  hours_per_day    hours running on a day it is used
  days_per_week    days used per week (default 7)
  quantity         number of identical units (default 1), e.g. 8 bulbs
  duty_cycle_pct   share of running time the motor/heater is really on (default 100;
                   fridges ~35-50, thermostatic heaters ~50-70)
  standby_watts    power when off but plugged in, per unit (default 0)
  kwh_per_year     energy-label figure per unit; replaces watts x hours when given
  offpeak_pct      share of running energy already used in off-peak hours (default 0)
  months_per_year  months in use, for seasonal loads like heaters or air conditioning (default 12)
Formulas:
  running kWh/day  = watts x quantity x hours x duty% / 1000 x days_per_week / 7 x months / 12
                     (or kwh_per_year x quantity / 365), averaged over the whole year
  standby kWh/day  = standby_watts x quantity x (24 - hours x days_per_week / 7) / 1000
  month = year / 12, year = day x 365; cost = kWh x rate (off-peak share x --offpeak-rate);
  standby is charged at the standard rate; the standing charge is listed separately.
Findings (severity):
  HIGH   STANDBY_SHARE    standby is >= 10% of all estimated kWh
  HIGH   BILL_GAP         estimate differs from --bill-kwh (monthly) by more than 25%
  MEDIUM BIG_CONSUMER     one appliance uses >= 25% of all kWh
  MEDIUM STANDBY_DEVICE   a unit draws >= 5 W on standby
  LOW    CHECK_DUTY_CYCLE fridge/freezer/heater running 24 h at 100% duty (likely overestimated)
  LOW    HIGH_WATTS       > 3500 W for an appliance that is not a known heavy load
Usage:
  python3 energy_cost.py appliances.csv --rate 0.32 --currency EUR
  python3 energy_cost.py appliances.csv --rate 0.32 --offpeak-rate 0.21 --standing-charge 0.40 --bill-kwh 260 --json
  python3 energy_cost.py --self-test
Exit code: 0 no HIGH findings, 1 HIGH findings, 2 bad input.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import io
import json
import sys

SEV_ORDER = {"HIGH": 0, "MEDIUM": 1, "LOW": 2}
HEAVY = ("heater", "oven", "stove", "hob", "cooktop", "dryer", "kettle", " ev ", "charger", "boiler",
         "water heater", "sauna", "heat pump", "air conditioner", " ac ", "furnace", "pool")
SHIFTABLE = ("wash", "dishwasher", "dryer", " ev ", "ev charger", "pool", "water heater", "boiler")
# keyword -> (idea, share of that appliance's running cost saved)
IDEAS = [
    (("bulb", "lamp", "light"), "replace with LED (about 85% less power for the same light)", 0.85, "watts>=25"),
    (("dryer",), "line-dry half the loads or switch to a heat-pump dryer (about 50%)", 0.5, None),
    (("water heater", "boiler"), "set to 55-60 C with a timer and insulate the tank (about 10%)", 0.10, None),
    (("space heater", "heater", "radiator"), "heat only the room in use and lower the thermostat 1 C (about 10%); a heat pump uses 2-4x less", 0.10, None),
    (("fridge", "freezer"), "set 4 C / -18 C, clean coils, check door seals (about 10%); a 15-year-old unit may use twice a new A-class one", 0.10, None),
    (("dishwasher",), "use the eco program and skip pre-rinsing with hot water (about 20%)", 0.20, None),
    (("washing machine", "washer"), "wash at 30 C instead of 40-60 C and run full loads (about 40%)", 0.40, None),
    (("kettle",), "boil only the water you need (about 25%)", 0.25, None),
    (("oven",), "use a microwave or air fryer for small meals (about 30%)", 0.30, None),
    (("pool",), "run the pump fewer hours or fit a variable-speed pump (about 50%)", 0.50, None),
    (("air conditioner", " ac ", "aircon"), "set 1-2 C warmer and clean filters (about 10%)", 0.10, None),
    (("dehumidifier",), "use a humidistat at 50-55% instead of running continuously (about 30%)", 0.30, None),
    (("desktop", "gaming pc", "computer"), "enable sleep after 15 minutes idle (about 20%)", 0.20, None),
]


class DataError(ValueError):
    pass


def num(row, key, default, line):
    v = (row.get(key) or "").strip().replace(",", ".") if isinstance(row.get(key), str) else row.get(key)
    if v in (None, ""):
        if default is None:
            raise DataError(f"line {line}: '{key}' is required")
        return float(default)
    try:
        x = float(v)
    except ValueError:
        raise DataError(f"line {line}: '{key}' must be a number, got '{v}'")
    if x < 0:
        raise DataError(f"line {line}: '{key}' cannot be negative")
    return x


def read_csv(text):
    first = text.splitlines()[0] if text.strip() else ""
    delim = ";" if first.count(";") > first.count(",") else ","
    rd = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text), delimiter=delim)
    if not rd.fieldnames or not {"appliance", "watts", "hours_per_day"} <= {f.strip().lower() for f in rd.fieldnames}:
        if not rd.fieldnames or "kwh_per_year" not in [f.strip().lower() for f in rd.fieldnames]:
            raise DataError("CSV needs columns appliance, watts, hours_per_day (or kwh_per_year)")
    items = []
    for line, raw in enumerate(rd, 2):
        row = {(k or "").strip().lower(): v for k, v in raw.items()}
        name = (row.get("appliance") or "").strip()
        if not name:
            continue
        label = (row.get("kwh_per_year") or "").strip()
        it = {"appliance": name,
              "watts": num(row, "watts", 0 if label else None, line),
              "hours": num(row, "hours_per_day", 24 if label else None, line),
              "days": num(row, "days_per_week", 7, line),
              "qty": num(row, "quantity", 1, line),
              "duty": num(row, "duty_cycle_pct", 100, line),
              "standby_w": num(row, "standby_watts", 0, line),
              "label_kwh": num(row, "kwh_per_year", 0, line) if label else None,
              "offpeak": num(row, "offpeak_pct", 0, line) / 100,
              "months": num(row, "months_per_year", 12, line)}
        if it["hours"] > 24:
            raise DataError(f"line {line}: hours_per_day {it['hours']:g} > 24")
        if it["days"] > 7 or it["duty"] > 100 or it["offpeak"] > 1 or it["months"] > 12:
            raise DataError(f"line {line}: days_per_week <= 7, months_per_year <= 12, duty_cycle_pct and offpeak_pct <= 100")
        items.append(it)
    if not items:
        raise DataError("no appliances in the CSV")
    return items


def has(name, words):
    low = " " + name.lower() + " "
    return any(w in low for w in words)


def estimate(items, rate, offpeak_rate=None, standing=0.0, bill_kwh=None):
    off = rate if offpeak_rate is None else offpeak_rate
    rows, findings, ideas = [], [], []

    def add(sev, code, msg):
        findings.append({"severity": sev, "code": code, "message": msg})
    for it in items:
        avg_hours = it["hours"] * it["days"] / 7
        if it["label_kwh"] is not None:
            run_day = it["label_kwh"] * it["qty"] / 365
        else:
            run_day = it["watts"] * it["qty"] * avg_hours * it["duty"] / 100 / 1000 * it["months"] / 12
        sb_day = it["standby_w"] * it["qty"] * (24 - avg_hours) / 1000
        run_cost_y = run_day * 365 * ((1 - it["offpeak"]) * rate + it["offpeak"] * off)
        sb_cost_y = sb_day * 365 * rate
        rows.append({"appliance": it["appliance"], "qty": it["qty"], "kwh_day": run_day + sb_day,
                     "kwh_month": (run_day + sb_day) * 365 / 12, "kwh_year": (run_day + sb_day) * 365,
                     "standby_kwh_year": sb_day * 365, "cost_month": (run_cost_y + sb_cost_y) / 12,
                     "cost_year": run_cost_y + sb_cost_y, "standby_cost_year": sb_cost_y,
                     "run_kwh_year": run_day * 365, "run_cost_year": run_cost_y})
        name = it["appliance"]
        if it["standby_w"] >= 5:
            add("MEDIUM", "STANDBY_DEVICE", f"{name}: {it['standby_w']:g} W standby per unit = {sb_day * 365:.0f} kWh/year; a switched power strip or unplugging saves {sb_cost_y:.2f}/year")
        if has(name, ("fridge", "freezer", "heater")) and it["label_kwh"] is None and it["hours"] >= 24 and it["duty"] >= 100:
            add("LOW", "CHECK_DUTY_CYCLE", f"{name}: 24 h at 100% duty; compressors and thermostats cycle, so set duty_cycle_pct (fridge ~40) or use the energy-label kWh/year")
        if it["watts"] > 3500 and not has(name, HEAVY):
            add("LOW", "HIGH_WATTS", f"{name}: {it['watts']:g} W is unusually high; check the nameplate (W, not mAh or VA)")
        for words, text, share, cond in IDEAS:
            if has(name, words) and (cond is None or it["watts"] >= 25):
                ideas.append({"appliance": name, "idea": text, "saving_year": run_cost_y * share,
                              "kwh_year": run_day * 365 * share})
                break
        if sb_cost_y > 0 and it["standby_w"] >= 1:
            ideas.append({"appliance": name, "idea": "cut standby with a switched strip or smart plug", "saving_year": sb_cost_y,
                          "kwh_year": sb_day * 365})
        if offpeak_rate is not None and offpeak_rate < rate and has(name, SHIFTABLE) and it["offpeak"] < 1:
            kwh = run_day * 365 * (1 - it["offpeak"])
            ideas.append({"appliance": name, "idea": "run in off-peak hours (timer or delay start)",
                          "saving_year": kwh * (rate - offpeak_rate), "kwh_year": 0.0})
    tot_kwh = sum(r["kwh_year"] for r in rows)
    tot_sb = sum(r["standby_kwh_year"] for r in rows)
    for r in rows:
        r["share"] = r["kwh_year"] / tot_kwh if tot_kwh else 0
        if r["share"] >= 0.25:
            add("MEDIUM", "BIG_CONSUMER", f"{r['appliance']} is {r['share']:.0%} of the estimated use ({r['kwh_year']:.0f} kWh/year); check it first")
    if tot_kwh and tot_sb / tot_kwh >= 0.10:
        add("HIGH", "STANDBY_SHARE", f"standby is {tot_sb / tot_kwh:.0%} of all use ({tot_sb:.0f} kWh/year, {tot_sb * rate:.2f}/year) - the cheapest saving to get")
    if bill_kwh:
        est_m = tot_kwh / 12
        gap = (bill_kwh - est_m) / bill_kwh
        if abs(gap) > 0.25:
            add("HIGH", "BILL_GAP", f"estimate {est_m:.0f} kWh/month vs bill {bill_kwh:g} kWh/month ({gap:+.0%}); "
                + ("missing appliances (water heating, electric heating, EV?) or hours too low" if gap > 0 else "hours or watts are too high, or some appliances are not used every day"))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: -r["kwh_year"])
    ideas.sort(key=lambda x: -x["saving_year"])
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: SEV_ORDER[f["severity"]])
    totals = {"kwh_day": tot_kwh / 365, "kwh_month": tot_kwh / 12, "kwh_year": tot_kwh,
              "standby_kwh_year": tot_sb, "energy_cost_year": sum(r["cost_year"] for r in rows),
              "standing_charge_year": standing * 365}
    totals["energy_cost_month"] = totals["energy_cost_year"] / 12
    totals["total_cost_year"] = totals["energy_cost_year"] + totals["standing_charge_year"]
    totals["total_cost_month"] = totals["total_cost_year"] / 12
    totals["savings_year"] = sum(i["saving_year"] for i in ideas)
    return rows, totals, findings, ideas


def render(rows, totals, findings, ideas, rate, cur, offpeak_rate, standing, top):
    c = (cur + " ") if cur else ""
    out = ["# Home appliance energy cost estimate", "",
           f"Tariff: {c}{rate:g}/kWh" + (f", off-peak {c}{offpeak_rate:g}/kWh" if offpeak_rate is not None else "")
           + (f", standing charge {c}{standing:g}/day" if standing else ""), "",
           f"Total: {totals['kwh_day']:.1f} kWh/day, {totals['kwh_month']:.0f} kWh/month, {totals['kwh_year']:,.0f} kWh/year; "
           f"energy {c}{totals['energy_cost_month']:,.2f}/month, {c}{totals['energy_cost_year']:,.2f}/year"
           + (f"; with standing charge {c}{totals['total_cost_year']:,.2f}/year" if standing else ""),
           f"Standby: {totals['standby_kwh_year']:.0f} kWh/year ({totals['standby_kwh_year'] / totals['kwh_year']:.0%})" if totals["kwh_year"] else "", "",
           "| Appliance | Qty | kWh/day | kWh/month | kWh/year | Standby kWh/yr | Cost/month | Cost/year | Share |",
           "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in rows:
        out.append(f"| {r['appliance']} | {r['qty']:g} | {r['kwh_day']:.2f} | {r['kwh_month']:.1f} | {r['kwh_year']:.0f} | "
                   f"{r['standby_kwh_year']:.0f} | {r['cost_month']:.2f} | {r['cost_year']:.2f} | {r['share']:.0%} |")
    out += ["", "## Findings"] + ([f"- {f['severity']} {f['code']}: {f['message']}" for f in findings] or ["- none"])
    out += ["", f"## Savings ideas (top {min(top, len(ideas))}, estimated)"]
    for i in ideas[:top]:
        out.append(f"- {i['appliance']}: {i['idea']} -> about {c}{i['saving_year']:.2f}/year" + (f", {i['kwh_year']:.0f} kWh" if i["kwh_year"] else ""))
    if len(ideas) > top:
        out.append(f"- ... {len(ideas) - top} more with --top {len(ideas)}")
    out += ["", "Estimates from rated watts and typical use; a plug-in energy meter or the smart meter gives real numbers. Savings overlap, so do not add them all up."]
    return "\n".join(out)


def self_test():
    results = []

    def check(name, cond):
        results.append(cond)
        print(("PASS " if cond else "FAIL ") + name)

    def run(csv_text, **kw):
        return estimate(read_csv(csv_text), kw.pop("rate", 0.30), **kw)
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day\nKettle,2000,0.5\n")
    check("1 kWh/day kettle", abs(rows[0]["kwh_day"] - 1.0) < 1e-9)
    check("365 kWh/year", abs(t["kwh_year"] - 365) < 1e-9)
    check("cost per year at 0.30", abs(t["energy_cost_year"] - 109.5) < 1e-6)
    check("month = year/12", abs(t["kwh_month"] - 365 / 12) < 1e-9)
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day,days_per_week,quantity\nWashing machine,1000,2,3.5,1\nLED bulb,9,5,7,6\n")
    w = [r for r in rows if r["appliance"] == "Washing machine"][0]
    check("days_per_week scales", abs(w["kwh_day"] - 1.0) < 1e-9)
    b = [r for r in rows if r["appliance"] == "LED bulb"][0]
    check("quantity scales", abs(b["kwh_day"] - 0.27) < 1e-9)
    check("LED idea skipped under 25 W", not any("LED" in x["idea"] for x in i))
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day,duty_cycle_pct\nFridge,150,24,40\n")
    check("duty cycle", abs(rows[0]["kwh_day"] - 1.44) < 1e-9)
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day,standby_watts\nTV,100,4,10\n")
    check("standby hours = 24 - use", abs(rows[0]["standby_kwh_year"] - 10 * 20 / 1000 * 365) < 1e-9)
    codes = [x["code"] for x in f]
    check("STANDBY_DEVICE", "STANDBY_DEVICE" in codes)
    check("STANDBY_SHARE HIGH", "STANDBY_SHARE" in codes)
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day,kwh_per_year,quantity\nFreezer,,,250,2\n")
    check("energy label kWh used", abs(t["kwh_year"] - 500) < 1e-9)
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day,offpeak_pct\nDishwasher,1200,1,50\n", offpeak_rate=0.15)
    check("off-peak share priced", abs(rows[0]["cost_year"] - 1.2 * 365 * (0.5 * 0.30 + 0.5 * 0.15)) < 1e-6)
    check("shift idea for rest", any("off-peak" in x["idea"] for x in i))
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day,months_per_year\nSpace heater,1000,4,6\n")
    check("months_per_year seasonal", abs(t["kwh_year"] - 4 * 365 / 2) < 1e-9)
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day,days_per_week\nDishwasher,1000,1,7\n")
    check("dishwasher gets eco idea, not washer idea", "eco" in i[0]["idea"])
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day\nHeater,2000,6\nTV,80,3\n")
    check("BIG_CONSUMER", any(x["code"] == "BIG_CONSUMER" for x in f))

    check("CHECK_DUTY_CYCLE LOW", any(x["code"] == "CHECK_DUTY_CYCLE" for x in f))
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day\nAquarium pump,5000,1\n")

    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day,standby_watts\nTelevision,90,4,0.5\nWater heater,2000,3,0\n", offpeak_rate=0.15)
    check("keywords: TV not shiftable, water heater gets tank idea", not any(x["appliance"] == "Television" and "off-peak" in x["idea"] for x in i)
          and any(x["appliance"] == "Water heater" and "tank" in x["idea"] for x in i))
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance;watts;hours_per_day\nHalogen lamp;60,0;4\n")
    check("semicolon + decimal comma", abs(rows[0]["kwh_day"] - 0.24) < 1e-9 and any("LED" in x["idea"] for x in i))
    rows, t, f, i = run("appliance,watts,hours_per_day\nTumble dryer,2500,1\n", standing=0.5)
    check("standing charge separate", abs(t["standing_charge_year"] - 182.5) < 1e-9 and abs(t["total_cost_year"] - t["energy_cost_year"] - 182.5) < 1e-9)
    check("dryer idea 50%", abs(i[0]["saving_year"] - 2.5 * 365 * 0.30 * 0.5) < 1e-6)
    for bad, name in (("appliance,watts,hours_per_day\nX,100,25\n", "hours > 24 rejected"),
                      ("appliance,watts,hours_per_day\nX,abc,2\n", "non-number rejected"),
                      ("name,power\nX,100\n", "missing columns rejected"),
                      ("appliance,watts,hours_per_day\nX,-5,2\n", "negative rejected")):

            read_csv(bad)
            check(name, False)

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Home appliance energy cost estimator")
    ap.add_argument("csv", nargs="?", help="appliances CSV")
    ap.add_argument("--rate", type=float, help="price per kWh (standard rate)")
    ap.add_argument("--offpeak-rate", type=float, help="price per kWh in off-peak hours")
    ap.add_argument("--standing-charge", type=float, default=0.0, help="fixed charge per day")
    ap.add_argument("--currency", default="", help="label, e.g. EUR, USD, TRY")
    ap.add_argument("--bill-kwh", type=float, help="actual monthly kWh from a bill, to compare")
    ap.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=8, help="savings ideas to show (default 8)")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.self_test:
        return self_test()
    if not a.csv or a.rate is None:
        ap.error("give a CSV and --rate, or --self-test")
    try:
        with open(a.csv, encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
            items = read_csv(fh.read())
        rows, totals, findings, ideas = estimate(items, a.rate, a.offpeak_rate, a.standing_charge, a.bill_kwh)
    except (OSError, DataError) as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if a.json:
        print(json.dumps({"appliances": rows, "totals": totals, "findings": findings, "ideas": ideas}, indent=2))
    else:
        print(render(rows, totals, findings, ideas, a.rate, a.currency, a.offpeak_rate, a.standing_charge, a.top))
    return 1 if any(f["severity"] == "HIGH" for f in findings) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

---
name: hiking-route-time-and-water-planner
description: Plans a day hike leg by leg. Estimates time with Naismith's rule and Langmuir's descent corrections, adjusted for terrain, fitness, pack weight and breaks, gives clock times for each leg, checks the finish against sunset and the latest safe start, and works out water to carry between refills and snacks to pack. Flags after-dark finishes, long dry stretches and hard terrain late in the day. Includes a stdlib Python planner with --self-test.
---

# Hiking Route Time and Water Planner

You help hikers turn a route into a realistic timetable: when they will reach each point, whether they finish in daylight, and how much water and food to carry. You show the rule behind each number, prefer conservative estimates, and always leave room for a slower day. You are not a substitute for local knowledge, a map or a weather forecast, and you say so when it matters.

## Files in this skill

- `scripts/hike_plan.py` - reads a legs CSV and prints a timetable, daylight check, water per stretch, food and findings (Python 3 standard library only)
- `references/time-rules.md` - Naismith's rule, Langmuir's corrections, terrain/fitness/pack factors, breaks and how to calibrate them
- `references/water-food-and-safety.md` - drinking rates, refill planning and water treatment, snacks, daylight margins, turnaround times and the safety checklist
- `templates/hike-plan.md` - the plan to share with the group and leave with a contact at home
- `examples/eagle-ridge-loop.csv` - a 22 km late-October loop with a scramble section and one refill point

## Workflow

### 1. Split the route into legs
Ask for the route (map app or guidebook), the date, and the group: pace, fitness, youngest or slowest member, pack weight. Split the route at summits, passes, huts, junctions and water sources; for each leg get the distance, ascent and descent (from the app's elevation profile) and the terrain type (road, path, rough, scramble, snow, bushwhack). Mark where water can be refilled. Get the sunset time for the date and place, and the forecast temperature.

### 2. Run the planner
```
python3 scripts/hike_plan.py examples/eagle-ridge-loop.csv --start 09:30 --sunset 17:20 --temp 24 --fitness 1.1 --pack-kg 9
python3 scripts/hike_plan.py my-route.csv --start 07:00 --sunset 20:45 --temp 31 --break-min 15 --json
python3 scripts/hike_plan.py --self-test
```
Exit code 1 means a HIGH finding (finish after sunset), 2 means bad input.

### 3. Adjust the plan
For AFTER_DARK or SMALL_MARGIN: start earlier (the script prints the latest sensible start), shorten the route, or pick a bail-out point and a turnaround time. For LONG_DRY_STRETCH: add a refill, carry more capacity, or move the long climb to the cool morning. For HARD_TERRAIN_LATE: reverse the loop so the scramble comes first. Explain the formulas from `references/time-rules.md` when asked, and suggest calibrating the fitness factor after the first leg.

### 4. Deliver
Fill `templates/hike-plan.md`: timetable with clock times, turnaround time, water and food list, bail-out options and the emergency details to leave with someone at home.

## Example result
For `examples/eagle-ridge-loop.csv` (22.2 km, +1170 m / -1150 m) starting 09:30 at fitness 1.1 and 24 C: 7h08 moving, 8h19 with breaks, finish about 17:49, which is 29 minutes after the 17:20 sunset (HIGH AFTER_DARK; latest sensible start 08:01). The first four legs have no water, so 4.4 L must be carried (MEDIUM LONG_DRY_STRETCH). Starting at 08:00 finishes at 16:19 with 61 minutes to spare; the water stretch remains, so the plan adds a 2 L bladder or a cached bottle at Pine Saddle.

## Rules

- Estimates are a starting point: tell the group to compare the real time on the first leg with the plan and rescale.
- Keep at least 60 minutes of daylight in hand, and a headlamp in every pack all year.
- Never suggest drinking untreated water; recommend filtering or treating any natural source.
- Weather, snow, river crossings and route conditions override any timetable: tell users to check the forecast and local reports, and to turn back when conditions change.
- Do not give medical advice beyond basic hydration and food guidance; point to first-aid training and local rescue numbers.

# Time Rules

## Naismith's rule (1892)
Allow 1 hour for every 5 km on the flat plus 1 hour for every 600 m of ascent (the original was 3 miles per hour plus 1 hour per 2000 ft).
```
moving minutes = distance_km / pace_kmh * 60 + ascent_m / 10
```
Example: 4.2 km with 380 m of ascent = 50.4 + 38 = 88 minutes before adjustments.

## Langmuir's corrections for descent
Naismith treats descent like the flat. Langmuir refined it:
- gentle descent, 5 to 12 degrees (about 9 to 21 %): subtract 10 minutes per 300 m of descent
- steep descent, more than 12 degrees: add 10 minutes per 300 m of descent
- under 5 degrees: no change
The script estimates the descent angle from the descent and the share of the leg's distance spent going down. It never lets a leg drop below half its flat time.

## Multipliers used by the script
| Factor | Value | When |
|---|---|---|
| Terrain road | 0.9 | Paved or forest road |
| Terrain path | 1.0 | Good footpath |
| Terrain rough | 1.25 | Rocky, rooty, loose or boggy path |
| Terrain scramble | 1.6 | Hands needed, exposed steps |
| Terrain snow | 1.5 | Soft or old snow without crampon work |
| Terrain bushwhack | 1.6 | No path, vegetation |
| Fitness | 0.85 / 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.4 | Fast and fit / average / relaxed or mixed group / young children |
| Pack | +2 % per kg above 10 kg | Overnight or heavy loads |
| Breaks | 10 min per hour (default) | Use 15 to 20 for photo walks, families, big groups |

Terrain multiplies the whole leg, including the climbing time.

## Calibrating
After the first leg, divide the real time by the planned time. If the group took 1h50 for a planned 1h37, the factor is 1.13: rerun with `--fitness` multiplied by that and check the finish again. Groups move at the pace of the slowest person; plan for them.

## Other rules you may meet
- Tranter's corrections: a fitness and fatigue table on top of Naismith, used for long mountain days.
- Tobler's hiking function: speed = 6 * exp(-3.5 * |slope + 0.05|) km/h, used in GIS tools; it gives similar totals on mixed routes.

## Turnaround time
For an out-and-back or a route with a bail-out, set a fixed turnaround time: the latest time you can leave the farthest point and still be back with an hour of daylight. Example: sunset 17:20, keep 60 minutes, the return takes 3h10 -> turn around by 13:10 wherever you are.
FILE:references/water-food-and-safety.md
# Water, Food and Safety

## Drinking rates used by the script
| Temperature | Litres per hour (total time) |
|---|---|
| under 15 C | 0.4 |
| 15 to 24 C | 0.5 |
| 25 to 29 C | 0.75 |
| 30 C and above | 1.0 |
Plus 0.1 L per 100 m of ascent, because climbing makes you sweat more. Needs vary a lot between people; heavy sweaters, children and people at altitude may need more. Drink a little often rather than a lot at once, and add electrolytes (salt tablets, drink mix or salty snacks) on hot days or when drinking more than about 3 L.

## Carry planning
- The start and every leg marked `water_at_end = yes` are refill points.
- Carry = largest amount needed between two refill points plus a 0.5 L reserve.
- More than 3 L (3 kg) is heavy; options are caching water, choosing a route past a hut or spring, or moving the hottest climb to early morning.
- Confirm that springs and huts actually have water at that time of year (many huts close in late autumn; springs dry up in late summer).

## Treating water
Treat all natural water: a hollow-fibre filter (bacteria and protozoa), chlorine dioxide tablets (also viruses, wait the full contact time, often 30 minutes, up to 4 hours for Cryptosporidium), UV pens for clear water, or boiling for 1 minute (3 minutes above 2000 m). Filter cloudy water through a cloth first.

## Food
About 200 to 300 kcal per hour on the move keeps energy steady on a long day: nuts, bars, dried fruit, cheese, sandwiches. The script uses 250 kcal per hour of total time. Pack one extra snack per person as an emergency reserve.

## Daylight
- Get sunset for the exact place and date (weather or astronomy apps). In mountains the sun leaves valleys and east-facing slopes earlier than the official time.
- Civil twilight gives about 20 to 40 minutes of usable light after sunset in mid-latitudes, less in the tropics. Do not plan to use it.
- Keep 60 minutes of daylight in hand (the default `--margin`). Every pack gets a headlamp with charged batteries.

## Safety checklist
- Forecast checked the evening before and the morning of the hike (thunderstorms, wind on ridges, freezing level).
- Route plan, start time, turnaround time and expected return left with someone at home, with who to call and when.
- Map offline on the phone, plus a power bank; paper map and compass on remote routes.
- Layers and a waterproof jacket, hat and gloves above the tree line even in summer, sun protection.
- Small first-aid kit, blister plasters, emergency blanket, whistle.
- Know the local emergency number (112 in Europe, 911 in North America) and the mountain rescue procedure.
- Rule: the group stays together and turns back at the turnaround time, at the first lightning, or when anyone is not feeling well.

FILE:scripts/hike_plan.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Hiking route time and water planner (Python 3 standard library only).

Reads a CSV of route legs and estimates moving time per leg with Naismith's rule
(5 km/h plus 1 hour per 600 m of ascent) and Langmuir's descent corrections,
adjusted for terrain, fitness and pack weight, then adds breaks, gives clock
times for every leg, checks the finish against sunset, and works out how much
water to carry between refill points and how much food to pack.

CSV columns (header required; ; or , separated):
  leg, distance_km, ascent_m, descent_m, terrain, water_at_end
terrain: road | path | rough | scramble | snow | bushwhack   water_at_end: yes/no

Usage:
  python3 hike_plan.py route.csv --start 08:30 --sunset 17:10 --temp 24
  python3 hike_plan.py route.csv --start 07:00 --fitness 1.2 --pack-kg 14 --json
  python3 hike_plan.py --self-test
Exit codes: 0 = plan fine, 1 = HIGH findings (finish after sunset), 2 = bad input.
"""
import argparse, csv, io, json, math, sys

TERRAIN = {"road": 0.9, "path": 1.0, "trail": 1.0, "rough": 1.25, "scramble": 1.6, "snow": 1.5, "bushwhack": 1.6}
REQUIRED = ["leg", "distance_km", "ascent_m", "descent_m", "terrain", "water_at_end"]
SEV = {"HIGH": 0, "MEDIUM": 1, "LOW": 2}


class InputError(Exception):
    pass


def num(v, field, row):
    try:
        x = float(str(v).strip().replace(",", "."))
    except ValueError:
        raise InputError(f"row {row}: {field} '{v}' is not a number")
    if x < 0:
        raise InputError(f"row {row}: {field} cannot be negative")
    return x


def hm(s):
    try:
        h, m = s.strip().split(":")
        h, m = int(h), int(m)
        assert 0 <= h < 24 and 0 <= m < 60
        return h * 60 + m
    except Exception:
        raise InputError(f"time '{s}' must be HH:MM")


def clock(mins):
    mins = int(round(mins))
    day, rem = divmod(mins, 1440)
    return f"{rem // 60:02d}:{rem % 60:02d}" + (f" (+{day}d)" if day else "")


def dur(mins):
    mins = int(round(mins))
    return f"{mins // 60}h{mins % 60:02d}"


def read_legs(text):
    sample = text[:2000]
    delim = ";" if sample.count(";") > sample.count(",") else ","
    rd = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text), delimiter=delim)
    if not rd.fieldnames:
        raise InputError("empty CSV")
    fields = [f.strip().lower() for f in rd.fieldnames]
    missing = [c for c in REQUIRED if c not in fields]
    if missing:
        raise InputError("missing columns: " + ", ".join(missing))
    legs = []
    for i, raw in enumerate(rd, start=2):
        r = {k.strip().lower(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in raw.items() if k}
        if not any(r.values()):
            continue
        t = r["terrain"].lower() or "path"
        if t not in TERRAIN:
            raise InputError(f"row {i}: terrain '{t}' must be one of {', '.join(TERRAIN)}")
        w = r["water_at_end"].lower()
        if w not in ("yes", "no", "y", "n", "1", "0", "true", "false", ""):
            raise InputError(f"row {i}: water_at_end must be yes or no")
        legs.append({"leg": r["leg"] or f"Leg {len(legs) + 1}",
                     "distance_km": num(r["distance_km"], "distance_km", i),
                     "ascent_m": num(r["ascent_m"], "ascent_m", i),
                     "descent_m": num(r["descent_m"], "descent_m", i),
                     "terrain": t, "water_at_end": w in ("yes", "y", "1", "true")})
    if not legs:
        raise InputError("no legs in CSV")
    return legs


def water_rate(temp_c):
    """Litres per hour of total time, before the ascent extra."""
    if temp_c < 15:
        return 0.4
    if temp_c < 25:
        return 0.5
    if temp_c < 30:
        return 0.75
    return 1.0


def leg_minutes(leg, pace_kmh):
    d, up, down = leg["distance_km"], leg["ascent_m"], leg["descent_m"]
    flat = d / pace_kmh * 60
    climb = up / 10.0  # Naismith: 60 min per 600 m
    descent_adj = 0.0
    steep = False
    if down > 0 and d > 0:
        horiz = d * 1000 * (down / (up + down))  # share of the leg spent descending
        angle = math.degrees(math.atan(down / horiz)) if horiz > 0 else 90
        if 5 <= angle <= 12:
            descent_adj = -down / 300 * 10   # Langmuir: gentle descent is faster
        elif angle > 12:
            descent_adj = down / 300 * 10    # steep descent is slower
        steep = angle > 14
    if up > 0 and d > 0:
        horiz_up = d * 1000 * (up / (up + down))
        steep = steep or math.degrees(math.atan(up / horiz_up)) > 14  # about 25 %
    return max(flat + climb + descent_adj, flat * 0.5), steep


def plan(legs, start, sunset=None, pace=5.0, fitness=1.0, pack_kg=8.0, break_min=10.0, temp=18.0, margin=60):
    if pace <= 0 or fitness <= 0:
        raise InputError("pace and fitness must be positive")
    pack_factor = 1.0 + max(0.0, pack_kg - 10) * 0.02  # +2 % per kg above 10 kg
    rate = water_rate(temp)
    t = start
    rows, findings = [], []
    stretch, stretches, stretch_legs = 0.0, [], []
    for leg in legs:
        base, steep = leg_minutes(leg, pace)
        moving = base * TERRAIN[leg["terrain"]] * fitness * pack_factor
        total = moving * (1 + break_min / 60)
        water = total / 60 * rate + leg["ascent_m"] / 100 * 0.1
        t_start, t = t, t + total
        rows.append({**leg, "moving_min": round(moving), "with_breaks_min": round(total),
                     "start": clock(t_start), "end": clock(t), "end_min": t, "water_l": round(water, 2), "steep": steep})
        stretch += water
        stretch_legs.append(leg["leg"])
        if leg["water_at_end"]:
            stretches.append((stretch, stretch_legs)); stretch, stretch_legs = 0.0, []
        if steep:
            findings.append(("LOW", "STEEP_LEG", f"{leg['leg']}: average gradient over 25 %; expect slower going than the formula and take care on the descent"))
    if stretch_legs:
        stretches.append((stretch, stretch_legs))
    moving_total = sum(r["moving_min"] for r in rows)
    total = t - start
    carry = max(s for s, _ in stretches) + 0.5
    for s, names in stretches:
        if s + 0.5 > 3.0:
            findings.append(("MEDIUM", "LONG_DRY_STRETCH", f"{' -> '.join(names)}: {s + 0.5:.1f} L to carry with no refill; add a refill, cache water or start earlier in the cool"))
    summary = {
        "distance_km": round(sum(l["distance_km"] for l in legs), 1),
        "ascent_m": round(sum(l["ascent_m"] for l in legs)),
        "descent_m": round(sum(l["descent_m"] for l in legs)),
        "moving_min": round(moving_total), "total_min": round(total),
        "start": clock(start), "finish": clock(t),
        "water_total_l": round(sum(r["water_l"] for r in rows), 1),
        "carry_max_l": round(carry, 1),
        "food_kcal": int(round(total / 60 * 250, -1)),
        "water_rate_l_per_h": rate, "pack_factor": round(pack_factor, 2),
    }
    if sunset is not None:
        left = sunset - t
        summary["sunset"] = clock(sunset)
        summary["minutes_before_sunset"] = round(left)
        summary["latest_start"] = clock(sunset - margin - total)
        if left < 0:
            findings.append(("HIGH", "AFTER_DARK", f"finish {clock(t)} is {dur(-left)} after sunset {clock(sunset)}; start by {summary['latest_start']}, shorten the route or plan a bail-out"))
        elif left < margin:
            findings.append(("MEDIUM", "SMALL_MARGIN", f"finish {clock(t)} leaves only {round(left)} min before sunset (target {margin}); start by {summary['latest_start']} and carry a headlamp"))
        for r in rows:
            if r["terrain"] in ("scramble", "snow") and r["end_min"] > sunset - 120:
                findings.append(("MEDIUM", "HARD_TERRAIN_LATE", f"{r['leg']} ({r['terrain']}) ends at {r['end']}, within 2 h of sunset; tired legs and fading light on hard ground"))
    if moving_total > 8 * 60:
        findings.append(("LOW", "LONG_DAY", f"{dur(moving_total)} moving time; check that everyone has done a day this long recently"))
    if temp >= 28 and any(l["ascent_m"] >= 300 for l in legs):
        findings.append(("MEDIUM", "HEAT", f"{temp:g} C with big climbs: start at first light, rest in shade, electrolytes with the water"))
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: SEV[f[0]])
    for r in rows:
        r.pop("end_min")
    return {"legs": rows, "summary": summary, "stretches": [{"legs": n, "litres": round(s + 0.5, 1)} for s, n in stretches],
            "findings": [{"severity": a, "code": b, "message": c} for a, b, c in findings]}


def to_markdown(p, args):
    s = p["summary"]
    out = ["# Hike plan", "",
           f"Settings: pace {args.pace:g} km/h, fitness x{args.fitness:g}, pack {args.pack_kg:g} kg (x{s['pack_factor']}), breaks {args.break_min:g} min per hour, {args.temp:g} C",
           "",
           f"Route: {s['distance_km']} km, +{s['ascent_m']} m / -{s['descent_m']} m; moving {dur(s['moving_min'])}, with breaks {dur(s['total_min'])}",
           f"Start {s['start']}, finish about {s['finish']}" + (f"; sunset {s['sunset']}, " + (f"{s['minutes_before_sunset']} min to spare" if s['minutes_before_sunset'] >= 0 else f"{dur(-s['minutes_before_sunset'])} AFTER sunset") + f"; latest sensible start {s['latest_start']}" if "sunset" in s else ""),
           "", "| Leg | km | Up m | Down m | Terrain | Moving | With breaks | Start | End | Water L | Refill at end |",
           "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in p["legs"]:
        out.append(f"| {r['leg']} | {r['distance_km']:g} | {r['ascent_m']:g} | {r['descent_m']:g} | {r['terrain']} | {dur(r['moving_min'])} | "
                   f"{dur(r['with_breaks_min'])} | {r['start']} | {r['end']} | {r['water_l']:.1f} | {'yes' if r['water_at_end'] else 'no'} |")
    out += ["", "## Water and food",
            f"- Drinking rate {s['water_rate_l_per_h']} L/h at this temperature plus 0.1 L per 100 m of climbing; total about {s['water_total_l']} L",
            f"- Carry at most {s['carry_max_l']} L (largest stretch between refills, incl. 0.5 L reserve); treat stream water"]
    for st in p["stretches"]:
        out.append(f"  - {' -> '.join(st['legs'])}: {st['litres']} L")
    out.append(f"- Food: about {s['food_kcal']} kcal of snacks (about 250 kcal per hour on the move), plus a spare")
    out += ["", "## Findings"]
    out += [f"- {f['severity']} {f['code']}: {f['message']}" for f in p["findings"]] or ["- none"]
    out += ["", "Estimates only: check them against your group's real pace on the first leg and adjust."]
    return "\n".join(out)


def self_test():
    res = []

    def check(name, cond):
        res.append(cond)
        print(("PASS " if cond else "FAIL ") + name)

    def L(d, up, down, terrain="path", water="no", name="x"):
        return {"leg": name, "distance_km": d, "ascent_m": up, "descent_m": down, "terrain": terrain, "water_at_end": water == "yes"}

    check("flat 10 km at 5 km/h = 120 min", round(leg_minutes(L(10, 0, 0), 5)[0]) == 120)
    check("Naismith 600 m climb adds 60 min", round(leg_minutes(L(5, 600, 0), 5)[0]) == 120)
    g = leg_minutes(L(6, 0, 900), 5)[0]  # angle ~8.5 deg: gentle
    check("gentle descent is faster (Langmuir)", round(g) == 72 - 30)
    st = leg_minutes(L(2, 0, 600), 5)  # ~16.7 deg: steep
    check("steep descent is slower and flagged", round(st[0]) == 24 + 20 and st[1])

    check("descent never below half the flat time", leg_minutes(L(10, 0, 1500), 5)[0] >= 60)
    p = plan([L(10, 0, 0)], hm("08:00"), break_min=0)
    check("finish time no breaks", p["summary"]["finish"] == "10:00")
    p = plan([L(10, 0, 0)], hm("08:00"), break_min=10)
    check("10 min break per hour", p["summary"]["total_min"] == 140)
    check("terrain multiplier", plan([L(10, 0, 0, "scramble")], 0, break_min=0)["summary"]["moving_min"] == 192)
    check("fitness multiplier", plan([L(10, 0, 0)], 0, fitness=1.2, break_min=0)["summary"]["moving_min"] == 144)
    check("pack over 10 kg slows", plan([L(10, 0, 0)], 0, pack_kg=15, break_min=0)["summary"]["moving_min"] == 132)
    p = plan([L(10, 0, 0)], hm("15:00"), sunset=hm("16:30"), break_min=0)
    check("AFTER_DARK HIGH", p["findings"][0]["code"] == "AFTER_DARK" and p["findings"][0]["severity"] == "HIGH")
    check("latest start", p["summary"]["latest_start"] == "13:30")
    p = plan([L(10, 0, 0)], hm("14:00"), sunset=hm("16:30"), break_min=0)
    check("SMALL_MARGIN", [f["code"] for f in p["findings"]] == ["SMALL_MARGIN"])
    check("no finding with time to spare", plan([L(10, 0, 0)], hm("08:00"), sunset=hm("18:00"))["findings"] == [])
    check("HARD_TERRAIN_LATE", any(f["code"] == "HARD_TERRAIN_LATE" for f in

    check("water rate by temperature", [water_rate(t) for t in (10, 20, 27, 33)] == [0.4, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0])
    p = plan([L(10, 0, 0, water="yes"), L(10, 0, 0)], 0, temp=20, break_min=0)
    check("water per leg", p["legs"][0]["water_l"] == 1.0)

    p = plan([L(10, 500, 0), L(10, 0, 500)], 0, temp=31, break_min=0)
    check("LONG_DRY_STRETCH and HEAT", {"LONG_DRY_STRETCH", "HEAT"} <= {f["code"] for f in p["findings"]})
    check("LONG_DAY", any(f["code"] == "LONG_DAY" for f in plan([L(45, 0, 0)], 0)["findings"]))
    check("food kcal", plan([L(10, 0, 0)], 0, break_min=0)["summary"]["food_kcal"] == 500)
    check("clock wraps past midnight", clock(1500) == "01:00 (+1d)")
    legs = read_legs("leg;distance_km;ascent_m;descent_m;terrain;water_at_end\nA;3,5;200;0;Path;yes\n")
    check("semicolon CSV + decimal comma", legs[0]["distance_km"] == 3.5 and legs[0]["water_at_end"])

                     ("leg,distance_km,ascent_m,descent_m,terrain,water_at_end\nA,1,-5,0,path,no\n", "negative"),
                     ("leg,distance_km,ascent_m,descent_m,terrain,water_at_end\nA,1,0,0,lava,no\n", "unknown terrain")]:
        try:
            read_legs(bad); check("rejects " + why, False)
        except InputError:
            check("rejects " + why, True)
    try:
        hm("25:00"); check("rejects bad time", False)
    except InputError:
        check("rejects bad time", True)
    passed = sum(res)
    print(f"{passed}/{len(res)} passed")
    return 0 if passed == len(res) else 1


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Hiking route time and water planner")
    ap.add_argument("csv", nargs="?", help="legs CSV")
    ap.add_argument("--start", help="start time HH:MM")
    ap.add_argument("--sunset", help="sunset time HH:MM")
    ap.add_argument("--pace", type=float, default=5.0, help="flat walking speed km/h (default 5)")
    ap.add_argument("--fitness", type=float, default=1.0, help="time multiplier: 0.85 fast, 1.0 average, 1.2 relaxed, 1.4 with young kids")
    ap.add_argument("--pack-kg", type=float, default=8.0, help="pack weight; +2%% time per kg above 10")
    ap.add_argument("--break-min", type=float, default=10.0, help="break minutes per hour of walking (default 10)")
    ap.add_argument("--temp", type=float, default=18.0, help="expected daytime temperature C")
    ap.add_argument("--margin", type=int, default=60, help="minutes of daylight to keep in hand (default 60)")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.self_test:
        return self_test()
    if not a.csv or not a.start:
        ap.error("give a CSV and --start, or --self-test")
    try:
        with open(a.csv, encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
            legs = read_legs(fh.read())
        p = plan(legs, hm(a.start), hm(a.sunset) if a.sunset else None, a.pace, a.fitness, a.pack_kg, a.break_min, a.temp, a.margin)
    except (OSError, InputError) as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    print(json.dumps(p, indent=2) if a.json else to_markdown(p, a))
    return 1 if any(f["severity"] == "HIGH" for f in p["findings"]) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Exam Revision Timetable Planner

You help students turn a stressful exam season into a realistic plan: which subject to study in each session, every day, until the last exam. You use evidence-based techniques (spacing, retrieval practice, interleaving, past papers), keep the plan humane with rest and sleep, and make the trade-offs visible when there is not enough time for everything.

## Files in this skill

- `scripts/revision_plan.py` - reads a subjects CSV and prints the subject table, a day-by-day timetable and findings (Python 3 standard library only)
- `references/study-techniques.md` - what to do inside a session: retrieval practice, spacing, interleaving, past papers, and what to avoid
- `references/scheduling-rules.md` - how the script assigns priorities, targets, session types and findings, and how to tune it
- `templates/revision-plan.md` - the plan to hand back: overview, weekly timetable, session routine, check-in points
- `examples/winter-exams.csv` - five university exams between 2 and 11 December with topic counts

## Workflow

### 1. Gather the facts
Ask for each exam: subject, date, how much it counts (credits, percentage of the final grade, or importance 1-5), confidence from 1 (lost) to 5 (solid), and the number of topics or chapters. Then ask for the first revision day, realistic hours on weekdays and weekends (after classes, work, commute), preferred session length (50/10 by default, 25/5 Pomodoro for low focus), a weekly rest day and any days that are already taken.

### 2. Run the planner
```
python3 scripts/revision_plan.py examples/winter-exams.csv --start 2026-11-16 --weekday-hours 3 --weekend-hours 5 --rest-day Sun --off 2026-11-21 --day-start 16:00
python3 scripts/revision_plan.py my-exams.csv --start 2026-05-04 --session-min 25 --break-min 5 --json
python3 scripts/revision_plan.py --self-test
```
Exit code 1 means a HIGH finding (fewer sessions than topics), 2 means bad input.

### 3. Fix the trade-offs
For UNDER_COVERED or TIGHT: add hours, start earlier, lower the target for strong subjects, or agree which low-yield topics to skim (use the syllabus weighting or past-paper frequency). For BACK_TO_BACK: move the second subject's practice before the first exam. Check the plan with the student: is it doable on a bad day? Leave slack rather than cramming every evening.

### 4. Deliver
Fill `templates/revision-plan.md`: the overview table, the timetable by week, the session routine from `references/study-techniques.md`, and two check-in dates to re-rate confidence and rerun the script.

## Example result
For `examples/winter-exams.csv` from 16 November with 3 h on weekdays, 5 h on Saturdays, Sundays and 21 November off: 25 days, 57 sessions of 50 minutes (47.5 h). Organic Chemistry (weight 5, confidence 2) and Microeconomics (4, 2) get 15 and 16 sessions, European History (3, 4) gets 6. Each subject ends with practice questions and a timed past paper the day before its exam. Findings: Statistics (10 sessions for 8 topics) and European History (6 for 6) are TIGHT, and European History and Microeconomics are BACK_TO_BACK on 7 and 8 December.

## Rules

- Plan with the hours the student really has, not the hours they wish they had; protect sleep (no sessions late at night before exams).
- Every session ends with retrieval (questions, blank-page recall, flashcards), not only rereading or highlighting.
- Keep at least one rest day or two half days a week; burnout costs more than one lost day.
- Re-plan after each check-in or exam instead of following a broken plan.
- Do not do graded coursework for the student; help with planning and study methods. If a student shows signs of serious stress or panic, encourage them to talk to student support or a doctor.

# Study Techniques

What to do inside each session. Ordered by strength of evidence (Dunlosky et al. 2013, "Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques", rated practice testing and distributed practice as high utility).

## Retrieval practice (high)
Bring information back from memory instead of reading it again: answer questions, write everything you remember on a blank page, then check against notes and fill the gaps in another colour. Flashcards work if you answer before flipping. Getting it wrong first and then correcting also helps learning.

## Spacing (high)
Spread sessions on a subject over many days instead of one long block. A simple review rhythm for each topic: the next day, after 3 days, after a week, then before the exam. The timetable interleaves subjects across days; start each session with 5 minutes of recall on the previous session of that subject to build the spacing in.

## Interleaving (moderate)
Mix problem types inside a subject (for maths and sciences: different kinds of problems in one set, not 20 of the same) so you practise choosing the method, which the exam requires.

## Past papers (high for exams)
Do at least one complete paper under timed conditions before each exam, then mark it with the official mark scheme and list the lost marks by topic. The script puts one on the day before each exam; add earlier ones if papers are available.

## Elaboration and self-explanation (moderate)
Ask "why does this work?" and "how does this connect to X?", explain a concept out loud as if teaching it, draw a concept map from memory.

## Low value on their own
Rereading, highlighting and copying notes feel productive but give little long-term gain. Use them only as a first pass before retrieval.

## Session routine (50/10 default)
1. 5 min: recall from memory what you did last time for this subject.
2. 30 min: learn or practise one topic (Learn + recall) or do questions (Practice questions).
3. 10 min: close the book and test yourself; mark what you missed.
4. 5 min: write down three questions you could not answer for next time.
5. 10 min break away from the screen: move, drink water.
For short attention spans use 25/5 sessions (`--session-min 25 --break-min 5`) and a longer break every four.

## Sleep, food and the day before
Sleep consolidates memory; all-nighters reduce exam performance. Keep the night before the exam for light review and sleep. Eat regular meals, move every day, and keep the phone in another room during sessions.
FILE:references/scheduling-rules.md
# Scheduling Rules

How `scripts/revision_plan.py` builds the timetable.

## Sessions per day
Sessions that fit in the daily hours: `floor((hours * 60 + break) / (session + break))`. With 50/10 sessions: 3 h -> 3 sessions, 5 h -> 5 sessions. Rest days (`--rest-day`) and `--off` dates have none. On an exam day only half the sessions are planned (the exam takes the rest), and only for later exams.

## Priority and target
- priority = weight x (6 - confidence). Weight 5, confidence 2 -> 20; weight 3, confidence 4 -> 6.
- target sessions = all sessions available before that exam x priority / sum of all priorities (at least 1).
Weight can be credits or a 1-5 importance score; only the ratios matter, so use the same scale for every subject.

## Choosing each session
For every session the script picks among subjects whose exam is still ahead and that have fewer than `--max-same` (default 2) sessions that day:
1. subjects still below their target first;
2. then a different subject from the previous session (interleaving);
3. then the highest remaining need per day left until the exam;
4. ties go to the higher priority, then the earlier exam.
The day before an exam starts with a timed past paper for that subject.

## Session types
- Learn + recall: until 60 % of the subject's target is done and more than 7 days before its exam.
- Mixed review: after 60 % of the target, more than 7 days out.
- Practice questions: in the last 7 days before the exam.
- Past paper (timed): the day before the exam.

## Findings
| Code | Severity | Rule | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| UNDER_COVERED | HIGH | sessions < topics | more hours, earlier start, skim low-yield topics |
| TIGHT | MEDIUM | sessions < 1.5 x topics | accept a single pass, or take time from strong subjects |
| BELOW_TARGET | MEDIUM | planned < 60 % of target | the exam is early; start that subject first |
| BACK_TO_BACK | MEDIUM | exams on consecutive days | front-load practice for the second exam |
| SAME_DAY | MEDIUM | two exams on one day | treat both as one block in the last week |
| NO_REST_DAY | LOW | plan > 10 days with no rest day or off days | add `--rest-day` |
| LONG_DAYS | LOW | more than 8 h a day | cap at 5-6 focused hours |

## Tuning
- More time for one subject: raise its weight or lower its confidence and rerun.
- Fewer subject switches: `--max-same 3`.
- Clock times: `--day-start 09:00` adds start and end times, with breaks between sessions.
- Re-plan: after each check-in, update confidence and `--start`, and rerun; finished exams drop out of the CSV.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exam revision timetable planner (Python 3 standard library only).

Reads a CSV of subjects with exam dates, weight and confidence, splits the
available study time into focused sessions, and builds a day-by-day timetable
that gives weak, heavy subjects more time, interleaves subjects, stops new work
on a subject after its exam, moves from learning to practice questions in the
last week before each exam and puts a timed past paper on the day before.

CSV columns (header required; ; or , separated):
  subject, exam_date (YYYY-MM-DD), weight (1-5 or credits), confidence (1-5), topics (optional)

Usage:
  python3 revision_plan.py exams.csv --start 2026-11-16 --weekday-hours 3 --weekend-hours 5
  python3 revision_plan.py exams.csv --start 2026-11-16 --rest-day Sun --off 2026-11-28,2026-11-29 --day-start 16:00
  python3 revision_plan.py --self-test
Exit codes: 0 = plan fits, 1 = HIGH findings (not enough sessions), 2 = bad input.
"""
import argparse, csv, datetime as dt, io, json, sys

DAYS = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]
SEV = {"HIGH": 0, "MEDIUM": 1, "LOW": 2}


class InputError(Exception):
    pass


def parse_date(s, what):
    try:
        return dt.date.fromisoformat(s.strip())
    except ValueError:
        raise InputError(f"{what} '{s}' must be YYYY-MM-DD")


def read_subjects(text):
    sample = text[:2000]
    delim = ";" if sample.count(";") > sample.count(",") else ","
    rd = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text), delimiter=delim)
    if not rd.fieldnames:
        raise InputError("empty CSV")
    fields = [f.strip().lower() for f in rd.fieldnames]
    missing = [c for c in ("subject", "exam_date", "weight", "confidence") if c not in fields]
    if missing:
        raise InputError("missing columns: " + ", ".join(missing))
    subs = []
    for i, raw in enumerate(rd, start=2):
        r = {k.strip().lower(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in raw.items() if k}
        if not any(r.values()):
            continue
        try:
            w = float(r["weight"].replace(",", "."))
            c = int(r["confidence"])
            t = int(r["topics"]) if r.get("topics") else None
        except ValueError:
            raise InputError(f"row {i}: weight, confidence and topics must be numbers")
        if w <= 0:
            raise InputError(f"row {i}: weight must be positive")
        if not 1 <= c <= 5:
            raise InputError(f"row {i}: confidence must be 1 (weak) to 5 (strong)")
        if not r["subject"]:
            raise InputError(f"row {i}: subject is empty")
        subs.append({"subject": r["subject"], "exam": parse_date(r["exam_date"], f"row {i}: exam_date"),
                     "weight": w, "confidence": c, "topics": t})
    if not subs:
        raise InputError("no subjects in CSV")
    return subs


def slots_for(hours, session, brk):
    """Number of sessions that fit in `hours` with a break between sessions."""
    mins = hours * 60
    if mins < session:
        return 0
    return int((mins + brk) // (session + brk))


def plan(subs, start, weekday_hours=3.0, weekend_hours=5.0, session=50, brk=10, rest_day=None,
         off=(), max_same=2, day_start=None):
    if session < 15 or brk < 0:
        raise InputError("session must be at least 15 minutes and break not negative")
    for s in subs:
        if s["exam"] <= start:
            raise InputError(f"{s['subject']}: exam {s['exam']} is not after the start date {start}")
    last = max(s["exam"] for s in subs)
    exam_days = {}
    for s in subs:
        exam_days.setdefault(s["exam"], []).append(s["subject"])
    for s in subs:
        s["priority"] = s["weight"] * (6 - s["confidence"])
    days = []
    d = start
    while d < last:
        if d in off or (rest_day is not None and d.weekday() == rest_day):
            n = 0
        else:
            n = slots_for(weekend_hours if d.weekday() >= 5 else weekday_hours, session, brk)
            if d in exam_days:
                n //= 2  # the exam takes half the day
        days.append((d, n))
        d += dt.timedelta(days=1)
    # target sessions: share of the slots available before each exam, by priority
    total_p = sum(s["priority"] for s in subs)
    for s in subs:
        before = sum(n for day, n in days if day < s["exam"])
        s["target"] = max(1, round(before * s["priority"] / total_p))
        s["planned"] = 0
    timetable = []
    for day, n in days:
        today, used = [], {}
        live = [s for s in subs if s["exam"] > day]
        # the day before an exam: a timed past paper first
        for s in live:
            if (s["exam"] - day).days == 1 and len(today) < n:
                today.append((s["subject"], "Past paper (timed)")); used[s["subject"]] = 1; s["planned"] += 1
        while len(today) < n:
            cands = [s for s in live if used.get(s["subject"], 0) < max_same]
            if not cands:
                break
            prev = today[-1][0] if today else None

            def score(s):
                days_left = max(1, (s["exam"] - day).days)
                need = (s["target"] - s["planned"]) / days_left
                # subjects still below target first, then interleave (avoid repeating the previous subject)
                return (s["planned"] < s["target"], s["subject"] != prev, need, s["priority"], -s["exam"].toordinal())
            s = max(cands, key=score)
            left = (s["exam"] - day).days
            kind = "Practice questions" if left <= 7 else ("Learn + recall" if s["planned"] < s["target"] * 0.6 else "Mixed review")
            today.append((s["subject"], kind)); used[s["subject"]] = used.get(s["subject"], 0) + 1; s["planned"] += 1
        timed = []
        t = day_start
        for subj, kind in today:
            if t is not None:
                end = t + session
                timed.append({"subject": subj, "kind": kind, "time": f"{t // 60:02d}:{t % 60:02d}-{end // 60:02d}:{end % 60:02d}"})
                t = end + brk
            else:
                timed.append({"subject": subj, "kind": kind})
        timetable.append({"date": day.isoformat(), "dow": DAYS[day.weekday()], "exams": exam_days.get(day, []), "sessions": timed})
    findings = []
    for s in subs:
        if s["topics"]:
            if s["planned"] < s["topics"]:
                findings.append(("HIGH", "UNDER_COVERED", f"{s['subject']}: {s['planned']} sessions for {s['topics']} topics; add hours, drop low-yield topics or start earlier"))
            elif s["planned"] < 1.5 * s["topics"]:
                findings.append(("MEDIUM", "TIGHT", f"{s['subject']}: {s['planned']} sessions for {s['topics']} topics leaves little time for a second pass"))
        if s["planned"] < 0.6 * s["target"]:
            findings.append(("MEDIUM", "BELOW_TARGET", f"{s['subject']}: {s['planned']} of {s['target']} target sessions fit before the exam"))
    dates = sorted(exam_days)
    for a, b in zip(dates, dates[1:]):
        if (b - a).days <= 1:
            findings.append(("MEDIUM", "BACK_TO_BACK", f"exams on {a} ({', '.join(exam_days[a])}) and {b} ({', '.join(exam_days[b])}); finish the second subject's practice before the first exam"))
    for day, subjects in exam_days.items():
        if len(subjects) > 1:
            findings.append(("MEDIUM", "SAME_DAY", f"{len(subjects)} exams on {day}: {', '.join(subjects)}"))
    if rest_day is None and len(days) > 10 and not off:
        findings.append(("LOW", "NO_REST_DAY", "no rest day in a plan longer than 10 days; take at least half a day off each week"))
    if max(weekday_hours, weekend_hours) > 8:
        findings.append(("LOW", "LONG_DAYS", "more than 8 hours of revision a day rarely stays productive; keep 5-6 focused hours"))
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: SEV[f[0]])
    total_sessions = sum(len(t["sessions"]) for t in timetable)
    return {
        "subjects": [{"subject": s["subject"], "exam": s["exam"].isoformat(), "weight": s["weight"], "confidence": s["confidence"],
                      "priority": s["priority"], "topics": s["topics"], "target": s["target"], "planned": s["planned"],
                      "hours": round(s["planned"] * session / 60, 1)} for s in sorted(subs, key=lambda x: x["exam"])],
        "summary": {"start": start.isoformat(), "last_exam": last.isoformat(), "days": len(days), "sessions": total_sessions,
                    "study_hours": round(total_sessions * session / 60, 1), "session_min": session, "break_min": brk},
        "timetable": timetable,
        "findings": [{"severity": a, "code": b, "message": c} for a, b, c in findings],
    }


def to_markdown(p):
    s = p["summary"]
    out = ["# Revision timetable", "",
           f"{s['start']} to {s['last_exam']}: {s['days']} days, {s['sessions']} sessions of {s['session_min']} min ({s['study_hours']} h of focused study), {s['break_min']} min breaks",
           "", "| Subject | Exam | Weight | Confidence | Priority | Topics | Target | Planned | Hours |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for x in p["subjects"]:
        out.append(f"| {x['subject']} | {x['exam']} | {x['weight']:g} | {x['confidence']} | {x['priority']:g} | {x['topics'] or '-'} | {x['target']} | {x['planned']} | {x['hours']} |")
    out += ["", "## Day by day", ""]
    for t in p["timetable"]:
        head = f"- **{t['dow']} {t['date']}**" + (f" (EXAM: {', '.join(t['exams'])})" if t["exams"] else "")
        if not t["sessions"]:
            out.append(head + ": rest")
            continue
        parts = [(f"{x['time']} " if "time" in x else "") + f"{x['subject']} ({x['kind']})" for x in t["sessions"]]
        out.append(head + ": " + "; ".join(parts))
    out += ["", "## Findings"]
    out += [f"- {f['severity']} {f['code']}: {f['message']}" for f in p["findings"]] or ["- none"]
    out += ["", "Start each session with 5 minutes of recall from memory on the previous session of that subject, and end with 3 questions you could not answer."]
    return "\n".join(out)


def self_test():
    res = []

    def check(name, cond):
        res.append(cond)
        print(("PASS " if cond else "FAIL ") + name)

    D = dt.date
    S = lambda name, exam, w=1, c=3, t=None: {"subject": name, "exam": exam, "weight": w, "confidence": c, "topics": t}
    check("slots: 3 h of 50+10 = 3", slots_for(3, 50, 10) == 3)
    check("slots: 50 min fits exactly 1", slots_for(50 / 60, 50, 10) == 1)
    check("slots: under one session = 0", slots_for(0.5, 50, 10) == 0)
    check("slots: 25+5 in 2 h = 4", slots_for(2, 25, 5) == 4)
    p = plan([S("A", D(2026, 1, 8))], D(2026, 1, 5), weekday_hours=2, weekend_hours=2, session=50, brk=10)
    check("no sessions on or after exam day", all(t["date"] < "2026-01-08" for t in p["timetable"]))
    check("day before exam starts with past paper", p["timetable"][-1]["sessions"][0]["kind"] == "Past paper (timed)")
    check("practice questions in last 7 days", all(x["kind"] != "Learn + recall" for t in p["timetable"] for x in t["sessions"]))
    subs = [S("Weak", D(2026, 3, 1), w=3, c=1), S("Strong", D(2026, 3, 1), w=3, c=5)]
    p = plan(subs, D(2026, 2, 1), weekday_hours=3, weekend_hours=3, max_same=3)
    pl = {x["subject"]: x["planned"] for x in p["subjects"]}
    check("weak subject gets more sessions", pl["Weak"] > 3 * pl["Strong"])
    check("priority = weight x (6 - confidence)", p["subjects"][0]["priority"] in (15, 3))
    p = plan([S("A", D(2026, 3, 1)), S("B", D(2026, 3, 1))], D(2026, 2, 1), weekday_hours=3, weekend_hours=3)
    check("max 2 sessions of one subject per day", all(
        sum(1 for x in t["sessions"] if x["subject"] == subj) <= 2 for t in p["timetable"] for subj in "AB"))
    check("subjects interleaved while both need time", all(t["sessions"][i]["subject"] != t["sessions"][i + 1]["subject"]
                                      for t in p["timetable"][:10] for i in range(len(t["sessions"]) - 1)))
    p = plan([S("A", D(2026, 2, 16))], D(2026, 2, 2), rest_day=6)
    check("rest day empty", all(not t["sessions"] for t in p["timetable"] if t["dow"] == "Sun"))
    p = plan([S("A", D(2026, 2, 6))], D(2026, 2, 2), off={D(2026, 2, 3)})
    check("off day empty", not [t for t in p["timetable"] if t["date"] == "2026-02-03"][0]["sessions"])
    p = plan([S("A", D(2026, 2, 5)), S("B", D(2026, 2, 9))], D(2026, 2, 2), weekday_hours=4)
    day5 = [t for t in p["timetable"] if t["date"] == "2026-02-05"][0]
    check("exam day: half the slots, other subject only", len(day5["sessions"]) == 2 and all(x["subject"] == "B" for x in day5["sessions"]))
    p = plan([S("A", D(2026, 2, 5), t=20)], D(2026, 2, 2))
    check("UNDER_COVERED HIGH", p["findings"][0]["code"] == "UNDER_COVERED")
    p = plan([S("A", D(2026, 2, 20), t=11)], D(2026, 2, 2), weekday_hours=1, weekend_hours=1, rest_day=6)
    check("TIGHT", any(f["code"] == "TIGHT" for f in p["findings"]))
    p = plan([S("A", D(2026, 2, 9)), S("B", D(2026, 2, 10)), S("C", D(2026, 2, 10))], D(2026, 2, 2))
    codes = [f["code"] for f in p["findings"]]
    check("BACK_TO_BACK and SAME_DAY", "BACK_TO_BACK" in codes and "SAME_DAY" in codes)
    check("NO_REST_DAY", "NO_REST_DAY" in [f["code"] for f in plan([S("A", D(2026, 3, 1))], D(2026, 2, 1))["findings"]])
    check("LONG_DAYS", "LONG_DAYS" in [f["code"] for f in plan([S("A", D(2026, 2, 5))], D(2026, 2, 2), weekend_hours=10)["findings"]])
    p = plan([S("A", D(2026, 2, 5))], D(2026, 2, 2), day_start=9 * 60)
    check("clock times with --day-start", p["timetable"][0]["sessions"][1]["time"] == "10:00-10:50")
    subs = read_subjects("subject;exam_date;weight;confidence;topics\nMaths;2026-12-03;4,5;2;9\n")
    check("semicolon CSV + decimal comma", subs[0]["weight"] == 4.5 and subs[0]["topics"] == 9)
    for bad, why in [("subject,exam_date\nA,2026-01-01\n", "missing columns"),
                     ("subject,exam_date,weight,confidence\nA,2026-13-01,1,3\n", "bad date"),
                     ("subject,exam_date,weight,confidence\nA,2026-01-01,1,9\n", "confidence out of range"),
                     ("subject,exam_date,weight,confidence\nA,2026-01-01,x,3\n", "non-number")]:
        try:
            read_subjects(bad); check("rejects " + why, False)
        except InputError:
            check("rejects " + why, True)
    try:
        plan([S("A", D(2026, 1, 1))], D(2026, 1, 1)); check("rejects exam not after start", False)
    except InputError:
        check("rejects exam not after start", True)
    passed = sum(res)
    print(f"{passed}/{len(res)} passed")
    return 0 if passed == len(res) else 1


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Exam revision timetable planner")
    ap.add_argument("csv", nargs="?", help="subjects CSV")
    ap.add_argument("--start", help="first revision day YYYY-MM-DD (default today)")
    ap.add_argument("--weekday-hours", type=float, default=3.0)
    ap.add_argument("--weekend-hours", type=float, default=5.0)
    ap.add_argument("--session-min", type=int, default=50, help="focused session length (default 50)")
    ap.add_argument("--break-min", type=int, default=10, help="break between sessions (default 10)")
    ap.add_argument("--rest-day", choices=DAYS, help="weekly day off")
    ap.add_argument("--off", default="", help="comma-separated dates with no revision (YYYY-MM-DD)")
    ap.add_argument("--max-same", type=int, default=2, help="max sessions of one subject per day (default 2)")
    ap.add_argument("--day-start", help="clock time of the first session HH:MM (adds times to the timetable)")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.self_test:
        return self_test()
    if not a.csv:
        ap.error("give a CSV, or --self-test")
    try:
        with open(a.csv, encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
            subs = read_subjects(fh.read())
        start = parse_date(a.start, "--start") if a.start else dt.date.today()
        off = {parse_date(x, "--off") for x in a.off.split(",") if x.strip()}
        ds = None
        if a.day_start:
            try:
                h, m = map(int, a.day_start.split(":")); assert 0 <= h < 24 and 0 <= m < 60
            except Exception:
                raise InputError("--day-start must be HH:MM")
            ds = h * 60 + m
        p = plan(subs, start, a.weekday_hours, a.weekend_hours, a.session_min, a.break_min,
                 DAYS.index(a.rest_day) if a.rest_day else None, off, a.max_same, ds)
    except (OSError, InputError) as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    print(json.dumps(p, indent=2) if a.json else to_markdown(p))
    return 1 if any(f["severity"] == "HIGH" for f in p["findings"]) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
